transcript.text:
Use the **List Accounts** endpoint with a filter on `identityId`:

```
GET https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/v3/accounts?filters=identityId eq "{identityId}"
```

### Example with cURL

```bash
ACCESS_TOKEN="<your_jwt_access_token>"
TENANT="your-tenant"
IDENTITY_ID="2c9180846e85e4b8016eafeba20c1314"

curl -X GET \
  "https://${TENANT}.api.identitynow.com/v3/accounts?filters=identityId%20eq%20%22${IDENTITY_ID}%22&limit=250&count=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```

### Getting your access token first (Client Credentials / PAT)

```bash
curl --location "https://${TENANT}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token" \
  --form 'grant_type="client_credentials"' \
  --form 'client_id="<PAT_CLIENT_ID>"' \
  --form 'client_secret="<PAT_CLIENT_SECRET>"'
```

Extract `access_token` from the response and use it in the `Authorization: Bearer` header.

### Pagination

If the identity has more than 250 accounts (unlikely but possible), page through results:

```bash
# Page 1: offset=0, limit=250
GET /v3/accounts?filters=identityId eq "{id}"&limit=250&offset=0&count=true

# Page 2: offset=250
GET /v3/accounts?filters=identityId eq "{id}"&limit=250&offset=250
```

The `X-Total-Count` response header (returned when `count=true`) tells you the total number of accounts so you know when to stop paging.

### Notes

- Use a PAT generated by an admin user to ensure access to all source accounts.
- Each account object in the response includes the source name, account attributes, entitlements, and current status (Enabled/Disabled/Locked/Pending).

```answer-summary

  - method: GET
    path: /v3/accounts
    api_version: v3
auth_flow: OAuth2 bearer token
required_scopes: []
key_parameters: [filters, limit, offset, count]
```
